bug_semantics: An XKB-capable local client can use XkbSetMap to replace a non-canonical key type with wire numLevels=255. CheckKeyTypes accepted every positive CARD8 width and stored it without enforcing XkbMaxShiftLevel=63. A later core ChangeKeyboardMapping reaches XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore; XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols derives groupsWidth from the attacker-controlled num_levels and uses XKB_OFFSET(g,l)=(g*groupsWidth)+l against a stack KeySym tsyms[XkbMaxSymsPerKey] buffer of 252 entries. With four groups and width 255, indices reach 1019, 767 entries beyond the buffer; the related fixed-size symbol/action temporaries make this a set of stack-overflow paths capable of server crash and, for a root X server, privilege escalation.
flaw_origin: The missing upper-bound validation, the fixed-size XKB temporaries, and their consumer path already coexist in the repository's 2003 R6.6 whole-tree baseline import ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1. That 609-file, 262690-line aggregate imported pre-existing XKB code (the affected files themselves carry 1993 Silicon Graphics copyright), so it is a public-history boundary rather than the smallest authoring commit. The 2025 CVE-2025-26597 fix 0e4ed94952b255c04fe910f6a1d9c852878dcd64 only added XkbResizeKeyActions(xkb,key,0) for a distinct zero-group stale-actions overflow and did not write this validator omission or sink; the 2026 advisory's 'incomplete fix' characterization therefore describes incomplete coverage, not causal introduction by that fix.
ai_marker: Unavailable for the true BIC because the line-level history ends at a wholesale import. The boundary commit object for ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 is author/committer Kaleb Keithley <kaleb@freedesktop.org>, timestamp 1068825294 +0000, message 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI marker; it is not treated as the BIC. The Claude Assisted-by trailer on the 2026 fix is deliberately excluded because AI-on-fix is not BIC evidence.
evidence: First-party advisory https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html states that X.Org Server before 21.1.23 and Xwayland before 24.1.12 are affected, identifies three stack overflows caused by unchecked non-canonical key-type shift levels, calls this incomplete coverage of CVE-2025-26597, and names 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e as the fix.

Run `git show --format=fuller --patch 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e`: its parent is bdd7bf57af208b1ddf57d4683d67104443b44812; the commit explains the SetMap -> stored numLevels=255 -> ChangeKeyboardMapping -> XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore -> XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols path and the 1019-versus-252 arithmetic, and changes only `if (width < 1)` to `if (width < 1 || width > XkbMaxShiftLevel)` in xkb/xkb.c. `git grep -n -F 'if (width < 1' bdd7bf57af208b1ddf57d4683d67104443b44812 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e -- xkb/xkb.c` displays the vulnerable and fixed predicates at the same line.

Run `git show 375d65aa2e47478331f407f5b95a4fef6200fc26:test/pyxtest/test_xkb.py` and inspect TestXkbSetMapNumLevels: the upstream regression reconstructs the attack by finding a key with a non-canonical type, setting its explicit bit if needed, sending XkbSetMap with num_levels=255, then ChangeKeyboardMapping; its comments identify tsyms[252], the 1019 maximum index, and the fixed rejection above 63.

Run `git blame -w -L 1648,1655 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e^ -- xkb/xkb.c`: whitespace-insensitive blame assigns `width = wire->numLevels` and `if (width < 1)` to ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1, rejecting the later 2012 formatting commit as an introducer. `git log main -L :CheckKeyTypes:xkb/xkb.c` walks the same predicate back through formatting/mechanical edits to that baseline import.

Run `git blame -w -L 214,244 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e^ -- xkb/xkbUtils.c` and `git log main -L :XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore:xkb/xkbUtils.c`: the fixed-size tsyms buffer and vulnerable conversion/copy path likewise trace to the 2003 baseline except for later initialization, signature, formatting, and linkage edits. `git log main -S 'XkbMaxSymsPerKey' -- xkb/xkbUtils.c xkb/XKBMisc.c` finds the baseline and a 2007 dead-code removal, not a later introduction.

Run `git grep -n -e 'width<1' -e 'tsyms\[XkbMaxSymsPerKey\]' -e 'XKB_OFFSET(g,l)' ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- xkb/xkb.c xkb/XKBMisc.c xkb/xkbUtils.c`: the baseline contains the incomplete lower-only validator at xkb/xkb.c:1712, XKB_OFFSET at XKBMisc.c:158, and fixed-size tsyms buffers at XKBMisc.c:656 and xkbUtils.c:291. `git grep -n -F 'Copyright (c) 1993' ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 -- xkb/XKBMisc.c xkb/xkb.c xkb/xkbUtils.c` shows all three imported files identify 1993 Silicon Graphics source.

Run `git show --stat --oneline --summary ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1`: it is 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line' and adds 609 files with 262690 insertions, including the complete xkb files, so it is an aggregate import and cannot be the smallest true BIC. `git ls-tree -r --name-only cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 xkb` produces no output, directly confirming that the import's immediate parent lacks the entire xkb tree; this does not establish parent absence for the unknown pre-import authoring commit, hence introducer_parent_absent=false.

Run `git cat-file -p ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1`: the boundary object has parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941, Kaleb Keithley as author and committer, the baseline message, and no trailers. This is documented only as the boundary-object check, not substituted for the required BIC-only marker check.

Run `git show --format=fuller --patch 0e4ed94952b255c04fe910f6a1d9c852878dcd64`: the direct CVE-2025-26597 fix changes only XkbChangeTypesOfKey's nGroups==0 branch by adding XkbResizeKeyActions; it neither creates nor modifies CheckKeyTypes's numLevels validation or the XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols indexing path.

Release boundary: `git grep -n -F 'if (width < 1' xorg-server-21.1.22 xorg-server-21.1.23 xwayland-24.1.11 xwayland-24.1.12 -- xkb/xkb.c` shows the lower-only check in 21.1.22 and 24.1.11 and the upper-bound check in 21.1.23 and 24.1.12. Stable equivalents are eced7e74cad4a46c3a3c17b2df13b70b8bedfc25 for server-21.1 and 72036644746c47a09eec106c367f186713fd606d for xwayland-24.1; `git tag --contains` starts at xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12 respectively. `git show --pretty=email 543e108516428fc8c3bea91d6563ad266f9a801e eced7e74cad4a46c3a3c17b2df13b70b8bedfc25 72036644746c47a09eec106c367f186713fd606d | git patch-id --stable` gives the same patch-id f063e9b8e69dc5b49718e8f6d59fc7ca5a7caa79 for all three.
reasoning: The security fix and upstream regression make the vulnerability and closing boundary unambiguous. Line history also makes clear that neither recent formatting nor the 2025 adjacent CVE fix authored the flaw: every necessary element is already present when the XKB source first appears. But the first appearance is a 262690-line R6.6 baseline import whose parent contains no xkb tree, while the files explicitly predate the import. Treating that aggregate as the BIC would violate the smallest-real-BIC rule, and there is no earlier commit object in the validated repository to decompose or inspect. Therefore the causal/AI audit is blocked at a genuine public-history boundary. The fix's Claude trailer cannot convert this to an AI-origin verdict because it is evidence only about the fix.
remaining_gap: The unavailable facts are the pre-import, line-level commit that first authored the lower-only CheckKeyTypes validation together with the vulnerable consumer assumptions, that commit's immediate parent, and that true BIC commit object's author/trailers. The validated public Git history begins with the non-decomposable 2003 R6.6 aggregate import, so these facts cannot be recovered from this repository; this is a BLOCKED history boundary rather than an obtainable EVIDENCE_GAP.
